skill.description: Guides developers through custom Moodle external web service APIs with validation, permissions, database access, service registration, testing, and troubleshooting.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, fenced examples, Moodle table names, placeholder URLs, and Moodle documentation links. No prompt-injection attempt or hidden automation was found in SKILL.md. Two content issues remain: debug logging guidance may expose sensitive data, and curl examples show command-line credentials.

remediation.issue: Debug logging guidance can expose sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Use restrictive directory permissions, redact SQL and stack traces, and enable detailed logs only for controlled development environments.

remediation.issue: Curl examples place credentials on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Use non-admin test accounts and avoid command-line passwords. Prefer documented token generation with redacted values or secure prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Debug Logging Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guidance creates a log directory with broad permissions and records SQL plus stack traces. Copied into production, this can expose sensitive data and allow log tampering.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 220 and 252-255 directly show permissive directory creation and detailed SQL or stack trace logging. The impact depends on deployment, so medium severity is appropriate.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exposure in Curl Testing Example
semantic_findings.description: The curl token example places an admin username and password directly on the command line. Shell history and process listings may expose credentials during testing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example uses placeholder values, but it explicitly demonstrates command-line credential submission for an admin user. The risk is practical during local testing.

content.value_statement: Moodle plugins need web services that follow the Moodle external API framework. This skill guides validation, permissions, database access, registration, testing, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains the three-method Moodle external API pattern: execute_parameters, execute, and execute_returns.
Shows service registration in db/services.php with function metadata, AJAX support, capabilities, and service bundles.
Provides examples for parameter validation, context checks, capability checks, and parameterized database queries.
Covers return structures for single values, nested structures, and arrays.
Includes testing paths through the Moodle web service client, curl, and core/ajax.
Lists debugging checks and common fixes for parameter, permission, cache, and transaction issues.
limitations: It is documentation guidance; it does not run Moodle tests or inspect a live Moodle instance.
Examples use placeholder plugin names, tables, users, courses, and URLs.
It does not replace a Moodle security review for production web services.
Version-specific details may need checking against the target Moodle release.

use_cases.title: Create a Course Reporting API
use_cases.description: Build a read-only Moodle service that returns course or quiz data with validated parameters and capability checks.

use_cases.title: Expose Data to an External App
use_cases.description: Plan REST or AJAX service registration for a mobile app, integration, or custom frontend.

use_cases.title: Test and Debug Web Services
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to diagnose missing functions, invalid parameters, permission errors, cache issues, and transaction problems.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Read API
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Moodle external API that reads course data. Include required parameters, permission checks, return fields, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Register a Web Service Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through registering a Moodle external API in db/services.php. Include function metadata, capabilities, AJAX support, and cache steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Permissions and Returns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Moodle API behavior. Recommend context validation, capability checks, parameter types, and return structures for safe access.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Complex Write API
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate a Moodle write API design that creates course activities. Check transactions, group restrictions, logging, error handling, and security risks.

output_examples.input: Build an API that returns quiz attempt counts by user and course.
output: A parameter plan for user ID and course ID.
Context and capability checks before database access.
A parameterized query approach and a matching return structure.
Testing steps for Moodle web services and AJAX callers.

output_examples.input: Register my plugin function for REST and AJAX access.
output: A service registration checklist with function name, class, method, type, capabilities, and AJAX setting.
Cache purge guidance after service changes.

output_examples.input: Review a write API that creates quizzes from categories.
output: A review focused on transactions, activity creation steps, group restrictions, and random question selection.
Risk notes for permissions, logging, and rollback behavior.
Testing recommendations for different Moodle roles.

best_practices: Validate every external parameter before business logic.
Check context and capabilities before reading or writing Moodle data.
Use parameterized database calls and keep write transactions short.
anti_patterns: Concatenating request values into SQL queries.
Registering services without clear capabilities or access restrictions.
Copying debug logging into production without redaction and restrictive permissions.

faq.question: What kind of Moodle APIs does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers custom external web service APIs for Moodle plugins, including read and write service patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete Moodle plugin?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on external API classes, service registration, validation, permissions, database access, and testing guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with Moodle REST services?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes registration and testing guidance for REST and AJAX access patterns.

faq.question: Does it address security checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes parameter validation, context validation, capability checks, and parameterized database queries.

faq.question: Can it debug live Moodle errors automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a troubleshooting checklist, but it cannot inspect a live server without user-provided context.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
